title: Galois group of a field component of a finite torsor
statement: Let K be a field [def-weil-field], G a finite group, and T a finite etale G-torsor over Spec K [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let E be a field with a K-algebra structure and let j:Spec E -> T.P be an open immersion satisfying j;T.pi = Spec(algebraMap K E). Then E/K is Galois and there is a subgroup H of G with a group isomorphism Aut_K(E) -> H. No connectedness of the entire torsor is assumed. This statement concerns a specified component; it constructs neither a decomposition of T nor its field factors and asserts no numerical divisibility.

source.place: Tags 03SF and 03QR; component of a finite torsor, finite separable fields and Galois sets

proof.text: Finiteness and etaleness of T over K imply that its coordinate ring is a finite product of finite separable fields (Mathlib Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod). Since Spec E is nonempty and connected, its open immersion into this finite discrete scheme identifies it with one component. Thus E/K is finite separable. Choose a separable closure Ks and an embedding sigma:E -> Ks. The geometric points of Spec E are the embeddings of E into Ks, forming a transitive absolute Galois set by finite_separable_extension_galois_classification [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification].

Use the geometric point determined by sigma and j as origin in the torsor fibre. The defining torsor isomorphism identifies this entire fibre with G under left multiplication. Absolute Galois automorphisms act on this fibre by precomposition and commute with this G-action. Consequently each gamma acts by right multiplication x -> x*c(gamma). Composition shows c(gamma*delta)=c(delta)*c(gamma); therefore rho(gamma)=c(gamma)^(-1) is a homomorphism. Its kernel N is the stabilizer of the chosen geometric point and every other point, hence is open and normal. Its image H is a subgroup of G, and the first isomorphism theorem gives Gal(Ks/K)/N isomorphic to H.

The stabilizer formula of finite_separable_extension_galois_classification [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] identifies N with the subgroup fixing sigma(E). The Galois fixed-field correspondence gives sigma(E)=Ks^N. Since N is normal, sigma(E)/K is Galois and restriction of absolute automorphisms gives Aut_K(sigma(E)) isomorphic to Gal(Ks/K)/N. Transfer along sigma.equivFieldRange and compose with the quotient-to-image isomorphism from the previous step. This proves both IsGalois K E and the claimed group equivalence. For the trivial group or any split torsor H is trivial and E is isomorphic to K; disconnected torsors are handled component by component.

lean.statement:
theorem field_torsor_component_galois_group
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G]
    (T : GaloisCover G (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra K E]
    (j : Spec (CommRingCat.of E) ⟶ T.P) [IsOpenImmersion j]
    (hj : j ≫ T.π = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K E))) :
    IsGalois K E ∧ ∃ H : Subgroup G, Nonempty ((E ≃ₐ[K] E) ≃* H)
